text: The sum of all natural numbers 1 + 2 + 3 + ... = -1/12 in Ramanujan summation. It appears in string theory.
A pizza that has radius 'z' and height 'a' has volume Pi × z × z × a.
There are exactly as many even numbers as there are natural numbers. Infinity is strange.
Euler's identity e^(iπ) + 1 = 0 connects five fundamental constants in one equation.
If you shuffle a deck of cards properly, the resulting order has almost certainly never existed before in human history.
'Mathematics is the queen of the sciences and number theory is the queen of mathematics.' — Gauss
A Möbius strip has only one side. Cut it down the middle and you get one longer strip, not two.
0.999... = 1 exactly. Not approximately. They are the same number.
The word 'algebra' comes from the Arabic 'al-jabr', meaning 'reunion of broken parts'.
There are more real numbers between 0 and 1 than there are natural numbers in total.
'Pure mathematics is, in its way, the poetry of logical ideas.' — Albert Einstein
The Banach-Tarski paradox: you can cut a sphere into 5 pieces and reassemble them into two spheres the same size.
Galois, who founded group theory, died in a duel at age 20 — after spending the night writing down his mathematical ideas.
A random walk on a 2D grid will return to its starting point with probability 1. In 3D, the probability is only about 34%.
'God made the integers, all else is the work of man.' — Leopold Kronecker
The number 1729 is the smallest number expressible as the sum of two cubes in two different ways: 1³+12³ and 9³+10³.
Every even number greater than 2 can be expressed as the sum of two primes. Nobody has proven this (Goldbach's conjecture).
The Fibonacci sequence appears in sunflower spirals, pinecone patterns, and galaxy arms. Nature loves this ratio.
There are infinitely many primes. Euclid proved this around 300 BC and the proof still fits in a paragraph.
'In mathematics the art of proposing a question must be held of higher value than solving it.' — Georg Cantor
The four color theorem — any map can be colored with just 4 colors — was the first major theorem proved by computer (1976).
If you could fold a piece of paper 42 times, it would reach the Moon. Exponential growth is wild.
Gödel showed that in any consistent mathematical system, there are true statements that cannot be proven.
The digits of π never repeat and never end. After trillions of digits computed, no pattern has been found.
'Mathematics is not about numbers, equations, or algorithms: it is about understanding.' — William Paul Thurston
A group of 23 people has a 50% chance that two share a birthday. With 70 people, it's 99.9%.
Emmy Noether's theorem links every symmetry in physics to a conservation law. Symmetry of time → conservation of energy.
The longest mathematical proof ever is the classification of finite simple groups: ~10,000 pages across hundreds of papers.
Ramanujan, self-taught in India, sent letters to Hardy with results so remarkable they changed number theory forever.
'Do not worry about your difficulties in Mathematics. I can assure you mine are still greater.' — Einstein
A Klein bottle is a surface with no inside or outside. It can only exist without self-intersection in 4D.
The Collatz conjecture is simple to state (if even, halve it; if odd, triple and add 1) but nobody can prove it always reaches 1.
2 is the only even prime number, making it the oddest prime.
Euler was so prolific that papers continued to be published for 50 years after his death.
'The essence of mathematics lies in its freedom.' — Georg Cantor
The harmonic series 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + ... diverges to infinity, but incredibly slowly. You need ~10^43 terms to reach 100.
Topology considers a coffee mug and a donut to be the same shape — both have exactly one hole.
The Mandelbrot set is generated by the simple formula z → z² + c, yet contains infinite complexity at every zoom level.
There are problems that are provably unsolvable — not just hard, but literally impossible for any algorithm (the Halting Problem).
'Mathematics, rightly viewed, possesses not only truth, but supreme beauty.' — Bertrand Russell
The digits 142857 × {1,2,3,4,5,6} produce cyclic permutations of themselves. It's called a cyclic number.
Cantor was so attacked for his work on infinity that he suffered depression. Today, his ideas are foundational.
P vs NP — whether problems that are easy to verify are also easy to solve — has a $1 million bounty.
The golden ratio φ = (1+√5)/2 ≈ 1.618 appears in art, architecture, and nature. It's the 'most irrational' number.
Andrew Wiles proved Fermat's Last Theorem in 1995 after working on it secretly for 7 years.
'An equation means nothing to me unless it expresses a thought of God.' — Ramanujan
The probability of a monkey randomly typing Shakespeare is not zero — just astronomically small.
Zero was independently invented in Mesopotamia, India, and Mesoamerica. It took Europe centuries to accept it.
e^(iτ) = 1 where τ = 2π. Some mathematicians argue τ is more natural than π.
'The only way to learn mathematics is to do mathematics.' — Paul Halmos
A sphere turned inside out (without creasing) is possible — this is Smale's paradox.
The Riemann Hypothesis, if proven, would reveal the deep pattern behind prime numbers. $1 million bounty.
In base 12, multiplication tables are simpler because 12 has more factors than 10.
Hypatia of Alexandria (c. 370-415 AD) was one of the first recorded female mathematicians and a renowned philosopher.
There are exactly 5 Platonic solids (tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron). This has been proven since antiquity.
'Mathematics is the music of reason.' — James Joseph Sylvester
The Monty Hall problem: switching doors gives you a 2/3 chance of winning, not 1/2. Even mathematicians got this wrong at first.
Fractals have fractional dimensions. The Koch snowflake has dimension log(4)/log(3) ≈ 1.26.
Hilbert's Hotel: a hotel with infinitely many rooms can always accommodate more guests, even infinitely many.
'The mathematician does not study pure mathematics because it is useful; he studies it because he delights in it.' — Poincaré
Gabriel's Horn has finite volume but infinite surface area. You can fill it with paint but never paint its surface.
Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm (for Babbage's Analytical Engine) in 1843, making her the first programmer.
The sum of interior angles of a triangle on a sphere is always MORE than 180°. Geometry depends on curvature.
There are 177,147 ways to tie a necktie, according to a mathematical analysis of knot sequences.
'If people do not believe that mathematics is simple, it is only because they do not realize how complicated life is.' — von Neumann
Nash equilibrium — the idea that earned John Nash the Nobel Prize — shows how rational agents can reach stable but suboptimal outcomes.
Euler discovered that V - E + F = 2 for any convex polyhedron. Vertices minus edges plus faces always equals 2.
The word 'calculus' comes from Latin for 'small pebble' — Romans used pebbles for counting.
A regular 17-gon CAN be constructed with a compass and straightedge. Gauss proved this at age 19, and it was so important to him that he asked for a 17-gon on his tombstone.
'There is no branch of mathematics, however abstract, which may not some day be applied to phenomena of the real world.' — Lobachevsky
Benford's Law: in many real-world datasets, the leading digit is 1 about 30% of the time, not 11% as you'd expect.
The Brouwer fixed-point theorem: stir a cup of coffee however you like, at least one molecule returns to its original position.
Turing proved that the Halting Problem is undecidable in 1936 — before electronic computers even existed.
i^i (where i = √-1) is a real number: approximately 0.2079.
'Mathematics knows no races or geographic boundaries; for mathematics, the cultural world is one country.' — David Hilbert
The number of possible chess games exceeds the number of atoms in the observable universe.
Fermat scribbled 'I have a truly marvelous proof' in a margin. It took 358 years for anyone else to find one.
The hairy ball theorem: you can't comb a hairy sphere flat without creating a cowlick. Earth always has a cyclone somewhere.
Every positive integer is the sum of at most 4 perfect squares. Lagrange proved this in 1770.
'The important thing in science is not so much to obtain new facts as to discover new ways of thinking about them.' — Bragg
If you pick a number at random from the reals, the probability it's rational is exactly 0.
The derivative of e^x is e^x. It's the only function (up to scaling) that is its own derivative.
Archimedes was killed by a Roman soldier while drawing geometric figures in the sand. His last words: 'Don't disturb my circles.'
ln(2) = 1 - 1/2 + 1/3 - 1/4 + ... This beautiful series converges to the natural log of 2.
A drunk person wandering randomly in 2D will eventually return home. In 3D they'll wander off forever.
The twin prime conjecture — infinitely many primes differ by 2 — remains unproven, despite massive progress since 2013.
'Life is good for only two things, discovering mathematics and teaching mathematics.' — Siméon Poisson
Gödel starved himself to death, fearing poisoning. Only his wife could convince him to eat — when she was hospitalized, he stopped.
